hypothesis: Question: among *constant* predictors (no voice signal at all), which central tendency of motor_UPDRS transfers to unseen patients, and does leave-one-training-patient-out (LOPO) ordering predict the development ordering? Prior qualified evidence: on development rows, the constant row-median reference (idea-baseline-0, loss 8.3794, group MAE 7.4265) still beats standardized Ridge (8.5229), HistGradientBoosting (10.4655), the patient-median between-patient ridge (idea-3f71f3, 8.3980) and the transductive within-patient drift method (idea-e196dc, 8.4757). So no measured method has yet extracted between- or within-patient voice signal that transfers. However, idea-e196dc's reported LOPO constant grid shows the pure row-mean constant at LOPO row RMSE 7.7122 / patient MAE 6.7122 versus the row-median constant at 7.8387 / 6.8661, i.e. roughly a 1.6% LOPO row-RMSE and 2.2% patient-MAE advantage for the mean under squared-error loss, obtained without any features. That grid was an internal by-product of a method whose dev score was worse than the median baseline, so it is only an untested internal comparison, not a transferred result. Contrasting pre-execution outcomes: (a) if the label distribution's mean-vs-median offset is a stable population property, the LOPO-selected constant (expected to be row_mean or the closely tied patient_mean_of_means) should improve development row RMSE by about 1-2% relative to 8.3794 while not worsening equal-patient MAE, which would identify the RMSE-optimal-constant choice as the only reliably transferring 'signal' so far and make LOPO a credible selector; (b) if the 7 development patients are skewed relative to the 28 training patients, the mean constant will be equal to or worse than 8.3794, which would be direct evidence that even a one-parameter LOPO preference does not transfer across a 7-patient group sample and would explain idea-e196dc's LOPO-to-dev reversal as group-sample noise rather than as a defect of that particular representation. Either result is informative and cheap; because default selection takes the lowest valid development row RMSE, a negative outcome cannot displace the existing median baseline. This is exploratory but one-factor: features, transduction and model class are all held at 'none' so only the constant's definition varies. Caveat retained: labels are linearly interpolated clinician ratings, so these constants describe the interpolated label distribution, not independent examinations, and 7 confirmation patients remain a small group-level sample.
